children: Iraq and neighboring Turkey have agreed to build a joint oil refinery in the Turkish Mediterranean transport hub of Ceyhan as part of a planned comprehensive pipeline deal next year.
Iraq and Turkey signed a provisional one-year agreement in late July to extend a 53-year pipeline pact, which Ankara had terminated in July 2025.
The pact governed Iraqi oil exports to Europe via Turkey through a 970-kilometre pipeline stretching from the Northern Kirkuk province to Ceyhan.

“In late July, Iraq and Turkey signed a temporary agreement for that pipeline as a prelude to a comprehensive agreement that will be signed next year,” said Ali Al-Shatri, director general of Iraq’s state organisation for marketing oil (SOMO).

“The new agreement will not be a mere pipeline pact as it will cover electricity, gas and other sectors…it also includes the construction of an oil refinery in Ceyhan to process Iraqi crude for export of refined products to Europe…we expect this project to generate more funds for Iraq along with the exported crude,” Al-Shatri told Iraq’s Alawla TV.
In June, Iraq said it has formed a government committee to negotiate a new oil pipeline agreement with Turkey before the expiry of the old pact on 27 July.
In July 2025, Ankara informed Baghdad that it had decided to terminate the pact governing the pipeline that carries Iraqi crude from Kirkuk to Ceyhan.
Turkey announced that the pact would no longer be in effect from 27 July this year and that a new agreement is needed.

“I think a refinery in Turkey is a good idea as it will allow Iraq to export refined products to Europe, where demand for such products is strong,” said Waleed Khaddouri, a well-known Iraqi energy analyst.

Al-Shatri said oil exports through the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline stood at around 180,000 bpd in August while Iraq’s total crude exports reached their highest level of 2.2 million bpd since the eruption of the Iran-US war in late February. The exports fetched the country around $4.5 billion in August, he added.
(Reporting by N Saeed; Editing by Anoop Menon)
